title: Embeddings and position
goals: Look up token embeddings and add explicit position vectors
Trace how token order changes a representation
Explain what a toy position scheme does and does not establish

prerequisite.prompt: Do adjacent vocabulary IDs prove that their tokens have similar meanings?
prerequisite.answer: No. IDs are indices. Similarity must refer to the embedding vectors and a defined comparison, not numerical ID distance.

vocabulary: A vector associated with a token under a specified model
A vector carrying information about a sequence position
The number of components in each vector

blocks.text: Use a two-token vocabulary: ID 1 means red with embedding [1,0]; ID 2 means blue with embedding [0,1]. This lookup table is constructed, not trained. The input red blue has embedding rows [1,0] and [0,1], so its shape is two sequence positions by two components. Reversing the text reverses the rows. ID 2 is not “twice as blue” as ID 1 is red.

A model needs a way to use order. A collection of vectors without any order-sensitive procedure may lose that distinction. We introduce one explicit toy scheme: add position vector [0,0] at position 0 and [2,0] at position 1. These invented values teach arithmetic; they are not a recommended production encoding.

The same red token now has [1,0] at position 0 and [3,0] at position 1. Both token identity and position affect the represented row. Addition requires equal widths; adding a three-component position vector to a two-component embedding violates the input contract. Record the position numbering and embedding-table version.

blocks.title: Keep the evidence roles separate
rows: Do not infer meaning from ID gaps
blocks.caption: The position contribution changes a token representation according to its location.

blocks.text: The elementwise sum of the represented rows is [3,1] for both red blue and blue red. This aggregate loses the row-order distinction despite the position additions. A later computation must actually use the represented rows appropriately; merely adding position vectors does not guarantee that every summary preserves order.

A position scheme may use learned values or a deterministic construction. The original Transformer added positional information to embeddings. Modern architectures can use other order-sensitive schemes. Our two-vector example demonstrates one possible mechanism and one information-loss failure, not all architecture choices.
Supported case: embeddings A=[2,1], B=[1,3], positions [0,0] and [1,-1]. Sequence A B becomes [2,1] and [2,2]. Sequence B A becomes [1,3] and [3,0]. Both sums are [4,3].

blocks.label: Guided: compute both ordered representations and compare their sums. Explain which operation discarded the difference.

blocks.text: State whether a vector is a token embedding, a position vector or their combination before calculating distances. Position changes can affect numerical similarity even for the same token. An unknown token or a sequence beyond the toy position table needs explicit handling. This two-position contract rejects a third position; it does not silently wrap back to position 0.

blocks.label: Exit: a program compares vocabulary IDs instead of vectors and silently repeats its two-position table for a longer sequence. Identify both contract errors.

workbook.title: Look up vectors
workbook.prompt: For red blue name the IDs, embedding rows and shape before adding positions.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: IDs [1,2]; rows [1,0],[0,1]; shape two positions by two components.

workbook.title: Add positions
workbook.prompt: Compute representations for red blue and blue red under the stated position table.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: red blue rows [1,0],[2,1]; blue red rows [0,1],[3,0]. Addition is component by component.

workbook.title: Audit the sum
workbook.prompt: Sum the rows for both sequences. Does the sum establish that the original text had the same order?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Both sums [3,1]. Summing discards the ordered-row difference; equal summaries do not prove equal source sequences.

workbook.title: Trace new vectors independently
workbook.prompt: Embeddings A=[1,2], B=[3,0], position 0=[0,1], position 1=[1,0]. Compute represented rows and sums for A B and B A. Explain what the equal sums mean.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: A B rows [1,3],[4,0]; B A rows [3,1],[2,2]. Both sums [5,3]; the summaries lose the ordering difference while the ordered row representations differ.

workbook.title: Handle a shape failure
workbook.prompt: An embedding has width two but its position vector has width three. The input also contains a third position absent from the table. Specify honest handling.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Reject mismatched vector widths and unsupported position explicitly. Do not truncate, wrap or invent values unless a separate documented contract defines that transformation.

teacher.background: Use two 45-minute sessions. All model outputs and probability tables are constructed classroom examples. No hosted AI service, external API or student account is needed. Distinguish a model objective from factual support and system permissions. Collect independent work before discussing its solutions.
materials: Printed lesson and workbook; paper and pencil
Prepare the independent task and fresh retry without displaying solutions
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and distinguish a numerical claim from its interpretation.
Read section 1 and complete W1; ask for a reason alongside each answer.
Trace the worked case in section 2 and complete W2.
Discuss the diagram and complete W3 in pairs; record support.
Complete the guided response before sharing the answer.
Read the remaining sections and trace another constructed case.
Collect W4 independently, requiring calculations and a bounded conclusion.
Discuss W5 and the exit response. Provide feedback and a fresh retry.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided: A B gives [2,1],[2,2]; B A gives [1,3],[3,0]. Both sums [4,3]. The summation discarded the row-order distinction. Exit: ID gaps are not vector similarity; repeating positions violates the stated table range.
misconceptions: A position vector guarantees every summary preserves order
The supplied sum counterexample loses the difference.
IDs select rows; vector components are separate data.
Any vector widths can be added
teacher.assessment: W4 requires both row pairs and shared sum [5,3], with an information-loss explanation. Fresh retry: A=[2,0], B=[0,4], positions [1,0] and [0,2]. A B gives [3,0],[0,6]; B A gives [1,4],[2,2]; sums [3,6].
teacher.support: Provide labelled intermediate columns and allow a calculator. Ask students to state the meaning and denominator of a value before interpreting it. Extension: implement the classroom calculation locally and test boundary cases without using personal data.
teacher.next: Week 6 introduces attention weights as a way to combine available value vectors for a specified query.
